description: Grilled Sea Bass Turkish Levrek is a staple of Turkish coastal cuisine, offering a light yet incredibly flavorful meal. Fresh sea bass is traditionally marinated with olive oil, lemon, and aromatic herbs, then perfectly grilled to achieve a tender, flaky texture. This simple preparation highlights the natural sweetness of the fish, making it a healthy and satisfying dish.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sea Bass
instructions.text: Rinse the whole sea bass under cold water and pat them very dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 diagonal slits on both sides of each fish. This helps the marinade penetrate deeply and ensures even cooking.

instructions.title: Mix the Marinade
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, fresh lemon juice, minced garlic, finely chopped parsley, salt, black pepper, and if using, the dried oregano and red pepper flakes. Mix until all ingredients are well combined.

instructions.title: Marinate the Fish
instructions.text: Place the prepared sea bass in a shallow dish or a large resealable bag. Pour the marinade over the fish, making sure to coat both the inside and outside, and gently rub it into the slits. Cover the dish or seal the bag and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours, allowing the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Preheat the Grill
instructions.text: Preheat your grill to medium-high heat, aiming for a temperature between 400-450 degrees F (200-230 degrees C). Clean the grill grates thoroughly with a wire brush and lightly brush them with a little olive oil to prevent the fish from sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Sea Bass
instructions.text: Carefully place the marinated sea bass directly onto the hot, oiled grill grates. Grill for 7-10 minutes per side, depending on the thickness of the fish. The fish is cooked when its flesh turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Avoid overcooking to ensure the fish remains moist and tender.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Once cooked, carefully remove the grilled sea bass from the grill. Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh lemon slices and a sprinkle of extra fresh parsley. Serve hot with a simple green salad or traditional Turkish mezes.

tips: For perfectly grilled fish, ensure your grill is very hot before placing the fish to prevent sticking and achieve a beautiful sear.
Always use fresh, high-quality sea bass. If levrek is unavailable, branzino or snapper can be good alternatives.
Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges, a simple green salad, and a side of Roka Salata for a complete Turkish meal.
